summary: Iteration 5 backend testing — 12/12 iter5 tests PASSED + 13/13 iter4 regression PASSED (1 pre-existing skip). All four P0/P1 production fixes verified: (1) SSE 2KB comment pad arrives in first chunk (first-byte <1s after CF; 2050-byte pad confirmed); (2) keepalive `:ping` comments flow; (3) full session→sources→token→done event flow intact; (4) POST /api/admin/qdrant/reset enforces all 3 guardrails (confirm=true required, collection allowlist, superadmin-only — 400/400/403/401); (5) BATCH=16 large-doc path ingests 100+ chunks cleanly with no processing_error; (6) ingest+chat end-to-end after `del file_bytes; gc.collect()` works. No backend regressions vs iter4 baseline.

minor.issue: X-Accel-Buffering=no header is set in code but stripped by Cloudflare before reaching client. Not a code bug — header is for upstream proxies (nginx/Envoy) which see it via internal hops. The functional defeat (2KB SSE comment pad in first chunk) is what actually disables buffering for clients; verified working. No action needed.

Form data `source="superadmin"` was overridden to `source="base_corpus"` on stored doc when uploaded by a superadmin user. This means superadmin uploads route to the base_knowledge collection regardless of the form value. Not a regression from this iteration, but worth confirming this is intentional — the qdrant/reset endpoint's docs-invalidation filter depends on this mapping (base collection ↔ source='base_corpus', company collection ↔ source!='base_corpus').

critical_code_review_comments: Good: chat_routes.py event_gen yields a 2052-byte `:` comment frame as the very first SSE write — verified pad ≥ 2048 spaces, first-byte < 5s through Cloudflare (test reported ~30-500ms on local re-runs).

Good: keepalive_pings task runs in parallel with the RAG stream via a shared asyncio.Queue + SENTINEL pattern; cancellation/await semantics in the `finally` block are correct (ping_stop.set + cancel + suppressed CancelledError).
Good: admin_routes.qdrant/reset uses asyncio.to_thread for the blocking qdrant delete+create calls — won't block the event loop during reset.
Good: qdrant/reset guardrails are tight: 400 without confirm, 400 on bad collection name (allowlist of two), 403 for non-superadmin (require_superadmin dependency), 401 without auth.

Good: vector_store BATCH=16 with gc.collect() + del intermediate buffers — 100+ chunk doc ingests cleanly (~30s end-to-end), no processing_error, chunk_count >= 100. Tested with 400 unique sections (UUID-tokenised to avoid dedup).
Good: After qdrant reset, /api/health/qdrant continues to return healthy — recreate path works.
Good: iter4 P0 event-loop responsiveness regression remains intact (test_event_loop_responsive_during_ingestion passes — health & login under 2s during concurrent ingestion).
Minor: Consider exposing the 2KB pad size as a module-level constant in chat_routes.py for clarity / future tuning.

Minor: The qdrant/reset `documents_invalidated` count returns motor's modified_count which can read 0 even when matched_count > 0 (if all matched docs already had the new values). Consider returning matched_count, or returning both for observability.

rca_of_the_issue.original_p0_production_bug: Chat answers never appeared in production. Three contributing root causes: (1) SSE response start was being buffered by Railway/Cloudflare/Envoy proxies until ~2KB of body data accumulated, delaying first-byte indefinitely for short streams; (2) Qdrant local on-disk index had become corrupted in ehs_base_knowledge ('operands could not be broadcast together') after Railway OOM-killed an in-flight ingestion; (3) Per-doc memory footprint during ingestion (BATCH=64 upsert + 300MB raw file bytes held in scope) was driving the Railway pod OOM that caused (2).
rca_of_the_issue.fixes_validated_this_iteration:
(1) chat_routes.py event_gen first yield is now `:` + 2048 spaces + 

 — first SSE frame is a comment pad that flushes proxy buffers immediately. Plus a parallel keepalive task emits `:ping

` every 2s to keep TCP/proxies happy. Confirmed via raw chunk inspection through Cloudflare. (2) New POST /api/admin/qdrant/reset?collection=<name>&confirm=true (superadmin-only) provides a safe operator path to wipe & recreate a corrupted Qdrant collection, then marks affected Mongo docs as not-processed so the UI prompts re-upload. All 3 guardrails verified. (3) vector_store.upsert_chunks BATCH 64→16 with explicit gc.collect() every 8 batches + del of intermediate buffers, and document_routes._process_document_bg now `del file_bytes; gc.collect()` after ingest. 100+ chunk doc still ingests cleanly. No event-loop regression vs iter4 baseline.
